Scope: The 0.2 line of the positional format. The baseline layouts here are the ones emitted by the unmodified 0.2.2 release; the layouts added by later CVS commits up to the abandoned CVS 0.2.3 tree are selected through SpiralPositionalText.history.json, which points back into this file for the unchanged plugins. Earlier layouts accepted by 0.2.2 StreamIn methods (pre-0.2.2 versions) are not yet catalogued.

Origin.Attribution: Derived from SpiralSynthModular by David Griffiths and contributors; see the preserved release AUTHORS and individual source notices.

LADSPA.Notes: Port arrays are separate, not interleaved. Identifier is the external LADSPA unique ID, not the native plugin ID. Plugin binary and port names are not embedded.

Matrix.Notes: Each pattern has sparse X,Y,Volume records in Y-major order. The -1 terminator contains X only; do not consume Y or Volume for it. Grid dimensions are 64 by 32.

MixSwitch.Notes: SwitchInputCount is total native inputs minus two.

Noise.Notes: Waveform is one raw byte: WHITE=0, PINK=1; it is not an ASCII number. Preserve embedded NUL in Source.

Oscillator.Notes: Reserved is the historical dummy float emitted as zero.

PoshSampler.Notes: Note is serialized twice. Preserve both fields; the historical reader overwrites Note with NoteRepeated. Audio is external, not in this state.

SpiralLoop.Notes: Audio sidecar is SpiralLoopSample26.wav, keyed by plugin type rather than instance in this release; multiple instances can collide.

SplitSwitch.Notes: SwitchOutputCount is total native outputs minus one.

Stream.Notes: FileName refers to an external path; decoding must not open it.

Rules: Fields arrays define byte-stream order. Object member order is not significant. Names label decoded historical fields, not current plugin property names.

Count uses FixedValue/Value or PropertyValue/PropertyName; exactly the selected value is non-null. PropertyValue resolves an earlier integer field in the containing object. Counts must be nonnegative and bounded by the decoder before allocation.
PluginState selects exactly one Plugins entry by PluginID in the containing Device. Its version field must match Equals. Empty Fields consumes no bytes, including no version token.
Until reads the first item field; when it equals the sentinel, consume only that field and finish the array without appending an item.

ByteString consumes its decimal byte count, exactly one separator byte, then exactly that many bytes including whitespace. Zero length still consumes the separator. Encoding is not guaranteed UTF-8; a JSON conversion must preserve undecodable bytes explicitly.
Retain source bytes and offsets for lossless decoding. Whitespace tokens alone cannot represent embedded spaces, newlines or the Noise NUL byte.

Unknown plugin IDs, unexpected versions, truncated strings or arrays and non-whitespace trailing data produce diagnostics and an opaque remainder. Retain complete preceding records; do not guess another layout or discard the entire decoded tree.
The file header version 4 does not uniquely identify application release 0.2.2. Select this historical profile explicitly until release discrimination is established.
No port names or topology schema were stored in this file. Wire port indices remain historical indices; mapping them to named modern ports is a separate migration step.
Comments are serialized in the historical device sequence using plugin ID -1. Moving comments into Patch.GUI and devices into Patch.Devices belongs to translation above the syntax reader.

Recovery.Validation: Validation diagnostics do not erase decoded items. Preserve invalid scalar values and unusable wires for inspection; patch construction decides whether a value can be applied or a wire installed.
Recovery.EnvelopeCounts: Treat DeviceCount and WireCount as advisory during recovery. Read complete device records until the -1 wire marker at a record boundary, and complete wire records until EOF. Report the original and observed counts. Never search inside an undecoded body for a marker.
Recovery.BodyCounts: Property-derived array lengths and byte-string lengths determine positional boundaries. Do not guess these lengths when invalid or truncated.
Recovery.PartialRecords: If a record cannot be decoded, preserve preceding complete records and the undecoded source bytes from the start of that record. Do not publish a partially decoded device or wire as complete.
Recovery.InvalidBoolean: Retain the raw numeric value with a diagnostic instead of coercing it to true/false or abandoning the patch.
Recovery.WireReferences: Retain wires with missing or ambiguous device IDs in the item tree and flag them as unusable. Patch construction must not dereference or connect them. Port compatibility requires separate validation.
Recovery.Limits: Recovery retains the same resource limits as ordinary decoding. Hitting a limit yields diagnostics and retained data rather than unbounded parsing.
Recovery.NoPatch: Empty or unrecognizable input has no loadable patch. Return an unreadable result and preserve source evidence; do not report a fabricated empty patch as a successful recovery.
